decision_conditions: a )Prior to the occupation of each Phase, a Post Completion Report for that phase setting out the predicted and actual performance against all numerical targets in the Circular Economy Statement prepared by Iceni Projects, shall be submitted to the GLA at: circulareconomystatements@london.gov.uk and the Local Planning Authority, along with any supporting evidence as per the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance. b) The Post Completion Report shall be approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, prior to the occupation of the development Phase to which it relates. Reason: To ensure that circular economy principles are incorporated in the design, construction and management of the approved development, including through minimising materials use and the sourcing and specification of materials; minimising and designing out waste at various stages; and by promoting re-usability, adaptability, flexibility and longevity.

a)	Notwithstanding the submitted information, prior to the commencement of Phase 2B, herby permitted, an updated Energy and Overheating Assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Energy Statement shall follow the energy hierarchy in the London Plan and be calculated through the Part L 2021 of the Building Regulations methodology SAP 10.2 and calculate the New Development Carbon Compensation Contribution to be paid for Phase 2B. b)	Notwithstanding the submitted information, prior to the commencement of Phase 3, hereby permitted, an updated Energy and Overheating Assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority for Phase 3. The Energy Statement shall follow the energy hierarchy in the London Plan and be calculated through the Part L 2021 of the Building Regulations methodology SAP 10.2. c)	The development shall be fully implemented in accordance with the approved details under part a) and b) of this condition prior to the first occupation of the relevant phase. d)	Following the practical completion of the final block in Phase 2B, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the final block in Phase 2B shall not be occupied until the updated Energy Statement has been approved. The updated Energy Statement shall reflect the measures taken in practice in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of the development and its services, as committed to in the design stage and shall calculate the Further New Development Carbon Compensation Contribution to be paid for Phase 2B. e)	Following the practical completion of the final block in Phase 3, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the final block in Phase 3 shall not be occupied until the updated Energy Statement has been approved. The updated Energy Statement shall reflect the measures taken in practice in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of the development and its services, as committed to in the design stage, for the development overall and shall calculate the Final New Development Carbon Compensation Contribution to be paid. Reason: to ensure sustainability and carbon reduction.

Prior to the occupation of each development phase, all residential units and non-residential space within the respective development phase shall be fitted with superfast broadband capability which shall be retained thereafter. Reason: To promote social inclusivity.

The Class E unit hereby approved shall achieve compliance with at least the BREEAM 'Very Good' standard in respect of WAT01 Water Consumption. Within 6 months of opening trade, the applicant shall submit the final BREEAM certificates to demonstrate the unit has achieved this requirement and be certified by the awarding body.Reason to ensure the development makes the fullest contributions to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Each dwelling (Use Class C3) hereby approved shall be designed to meet a target of 105litres or less per head per day.Reason: in order to protect and conserve water supplied and resources.

The development hereby permitted shall be built out in strict accordance with the Fire Strategy and Gateway One Forms dated July 2024 prepared by Ashton Fire. A revised Fire Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority should any further assessment be carried out, if necessary, where modifications occur. Reason: In order to achieve the highest standards of fire safety and ensure the safety of all building users.

All lifts within buildings hereby approved, forming a development Phase, shall be installed and operational prior to the first occupation of the respective buildings in that development Phase.Reason: To ensure that inclusive and accessible routes are provided throughout the floorspace at all floors and also accessible routes through the site are provided.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved plans, the construction of blocks located within Phase 2b and 3 of the hereby permitted development shall not progress beyond podium slab level, until revised details of wind mitigation to the Street Level and Elevated Levels for the respective block has first been submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. The revised details shall be in accordance with Chapter 10 'Wind Microclimate' of the Alma Estate Phases 2B and 3 Environmental Statement, July 2024 and are to include but not limited to measures to ensure no adverse wind conditions to:i.	The top-floor balconies on the west and southwest sides of the Phase 2B tower;ii.	balconies on the southeast and north sides of the Phase 3 tower;iii.	proposed gates (receptors 162 and 174);iv.	proposed balconies located at the west side of Phase 2B;v.	proposed seating areas, (receptors 214, 215, 217, 218, 220, and 222);vi.	top-floor balconies on the west and southwest sides of the Phase 2B tower;vii.	the top levels balconies of the Phase 3 tower; andviii.	details of measures to address noise levels and wind microclimate.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so agreed and shall be retained as such thereafter.Reason:  To ensure that the development achieves safe, comfortable and attractive amenity spaces.

10% of dwellings in the development hereby approved shall comply with Building Regulations Optional Requirement Approved Documents (M4) (3) Category 3: wheelchair accessible or easily adaptable dwellings (2015 edition). 90% of units shall achieve M4(2). Evidence of compliance shall be notified to the building control body to check compliance.Reason: To ensure homes are accessible and adaptable.

1. Prior to the commencement of any Phase in the development hereby permitted (excluding demolition and below ground works), details of the measures to be incorporated into the development demonstrating how the principles and practices of the 'Secured by Design' scheme and local crime prevention measures have been included for each Phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Once approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Metropolitan Police Designing Out Crime Officers, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed details and maintained thereafter.2. Prior to the first occupation, or use of an individual building within each phase of the development, a letter from Metropolitan Police Designing Out Crime Office stating that appropriate SBD measures of compliance for the occupied or used section have been met, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 3. On completion of the development including landscaping, external materials and other works incidental to the proposed development, the SBD certificate or a letter from Metropolitan Police Designing Out Crime Office stating that appropriate SBD measures of compliance for the whole site shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interest of creating safer, secure, sustainable communities.

Prior to the commencement of development in each Phase, a method statement shall be submitted to an approved by the Local Planning Authority, detailing retained trees within that Phase (including the retention of trees T8, T10, T11 and T12) and any trees on adjacent land (as shown in Arboricultural  Impact Assessment & Method Statement (RPS, July 2024 REV00) shall be protected in accordance with BS5837:2012, with any tree work to be carried out in accordance with BS3998:2010 - Tree Work - Recommendations. The protection shall be retained intact for the full duration of the development within that development Phase until all equipment and materials have been removed from site. If the protection is damaged, all operations shall cease until it is repaired in accordance with the approved details. Nothing shall be stored or placed in any protected area in accordance with this condition and the ground levels within those areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavations be made without the written approval of the local authority. Reason: To make sure that the trees on the site are adequately protected during building works and in the interests of visual amenity and biodiversity.

a.	No development shall take place, including any ground works or demolition in any Phase, until a copy of the results of additional survey work undertaken has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. b.	If any additional surveys identify works requiring a license from Natural England in relation to bat roosts that will be impacted, no works to any affected areas shall commence until a copy of the license is submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The works shall then be carried out in accordance with the agreed licence.c.	No development, including vegetation removal and demolition, shall commence until a Biodiversity Mitigation and Enhancement Plan in accordance with the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal and Preliminary Bat Roost Assessment (July 2024) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority detailing such measures. The plan shall include, but not be limited to, the location and specification of bird and bat boxes.Reason: To ensure that appropriate measures are undertaken to ensure any disturbance to protected bat and bird species.

Before each Phase is first occupied, or brought into use, details of any external lighting and any internal lighting within communal areas shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be completed in accordance with the approved details before it is first occupied or brought into use. Reason: to ensure satisfactory design and in the interests of resident's amenity.

Prior to the occupation of each development Phase containing car parking, a car parking management plan for that Phase shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan should include:a) Car park plan with clearly marked out bays for residents, loading/unloading, visitors, accessible parking bays, and parking bays for Car Clubs, as appropriate; b) Details of the siting, type and design of charging points, the energy sources and the strategy/management plan of supplying and maintaining Electric Vehicle Charging Points including the mechanism for making passive provision active to ensure that a minimum of 20% or residential car parking spaces are provided with Electric Charging Points and the remaining 80% of residential car parking spaces include passive provision for electric vehicles in the future);c) Contact details (telephone/ email/ name) of a person/company responsible for managing the car parking bay(s); d) Proposed parking controls to keep clear the turning areas for delivery/service vehicles; e) Proposals for the management of the risk of overspill parking; f) enforcement regime proposed; g) details of frequency and strategy of reviewing by an individual/organisation (including contact details); h) Maintenance regime for apparatus/furniture/lighting etc.; i) Details of parking charges/fees; j) Number of 'accessible'/disabled bays, their distribution, and details of monitoring of their take up and how it connects with the any relevant Travel Plan(s), and; k) Proposed of car parking space allocation strategy within the respective development Phase (first come first served basis, etc)The approved details shall be implemented prior to occupation of the relevant Phase and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure an appropriate level of car parking is provided for the relevant units and that this is allocated to be convenient and accessible for future residents and users.

The approved quantum of short and long-term cycle parking spaces set out within the Transport Statement prepared by Iceni Projects, shall be provided and made operational prior to the first occupation of any dwellings and/or non-residential units in the Phase to which they relate and shall be retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure an acceptable level of residential and commercial cycle parking spaces.

a.	Prior to occupation of each development Phase, a Delivery and Servicing Plan for the relevant Phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall in incorporate details of deliveries to the site and serving arrangements including the size and type of vehicles, expected frequencies, loading/unloading locations and any details of highway markings, signage and controls, management measures, and access routes. The Plan shall also identify efficiencies and sustainability measures to be undertaken once the development is operational in relation to deliveries and servicing. b.	The approved Plan shall be implemented on occupation of the relevant development Phase and adhered to thereafter. Reason: To ensure adequate serving of the proposed buildings and in the interest of highway safety.

No development approved by this planning permission shall commence until a remediation strategy to deal with the risks associated with contamination of the site in respect of the development hereby permitted, has been submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. This strategy will include the following components: 1) A site investigation scheme, based on the previously submitted Preliminary Risk Assessment (PRA) dated July 2024 (ref: ALM-WSP-XX-XX-AS-O-00001) to provide information for a detailed assessment of the risk to all receptors that may be affected, including those off-site. 2) The results of the site investigation and the detailed risk assessment referred to in (1) and, based on these, an options appraisal and remediation strategy giving full details of the remediation measures required and how they are to be undertaken. 3) A verification plan providing details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy in (2) are complete and identifying any requirements for longer-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action. Any changes to these components require the written consent of the local planning authority. The scheme shall be implemented as approved. Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, and is not put at, unacceptable risk from adversely affected unacceptable levels of water pollution.

If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved. Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to and is not put at unacceptable risk from or adversely affected by unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site.

The development hereby permitted shall not commence until a monitoring and maintenance plan in respect of contamination, including a timetable of monitoring and submission of reports to the local planning authority, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. Reports as specified in the approved plan, including details of any necessary contingency action arising from the monitoring, shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to the water environment by managing any ongoing contamination issues and completing all necessary long-term remediation measures.

A scheme for managing any borehole installed for the investigation of soils, groundwater or geotechnical purposes shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall provide details of how redundant boreholes are to be decommissioned and how any boreholes that need to be retained, post-development, for monitoring purposes will be secured, protected and inspected. The scheme as approved shall be implemented prior to the occupation of each phase of development. Reason: To ensure that redundant boreholes are safe and secure, and do not cause groundwater pollution.

Prior to any part of the permitted development being brought into use, a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation strategy and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met. Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete.

Piling, deep foundations, or other intrusive groundworks (investigation boreholes/tunnel shafts/ground source heating and cooling systems) using penetrative methods shall not be carried out other than with the written consent of the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not harm groundwater resources in line with the Environment Agency's approach to groundwater protection.

No drainage systems for the infiltration of surface water to the ground are permitted other than with the written consent of the local planning authority. Any proposals for such systems must be supported by an assessment of the risks to controlled waters. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to and is not put at unacceptable risk from or adversely affected by unacceptable levels of water pollution caused by mobilised contaminants.

No development shall take place until measures to reduce or offset the air quality impacts of building emissions from the site to ensure the site would be classed as air quality neutral, are submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. Once approved the measures shall be fully implemented at the development. Where offsetting is not possible an offsetting payment shall be made; an offsetting calculation should be undertaken in accordance with GLA Air Quality Neutral guidance taking into consideration the finalised design of the Proposed Development by way of a section 106 agreement.Reason:  To protect residents from poor air quality.

Occupation of the development in a Phase shall not take place until an acoustic report, written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the mechanical plant and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the mechanical plant does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest or most noise affected residential properties.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance.

Prior to commencement of the relevant works, details of the design of covered cycle parking within Phase 2b shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained for cycle parking.Reason: To ensure the external appearance of the development is appropriate to the locality and promotes high quality design.

The development shall be completed in reasonable accordance with the recommendations in the Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment, prepared by RPS and the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal and Preliminary Bat Roost Assessment, prepared by RPS and achieve a minimum of 10% Biodiversity Net Gain. All the recommendations shall be implemented in full within the timescales laid out in the recommendations, unless otherwise updated by way of a Biodiversity Gain Plan to be agreed in writing by the local planning authority, and thereafter maintained for a minimum of 30 years for the stated purposes of biodiversity conservation.Reason: In the interests of improving and maintain biodiversity.

Prior to the commencement of development above slab level of any Phase, details of both hard and soft landscape works shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and timetable. The details submitted shall reflect the measures set out in the Urban Greening Factor calculation to achieve a score of at least 0.4 across the wider site and shall include: 1.	Soft landscaping, including any grass and turf areas, trees, planters, shrubs and herbaceous areas including details of species, sizes number, densities and sections of landscaped areas; 2.	A Tree Planting Statement providing full details, locations, specifications and construction methods for all purpose-built tree pits and associated ground features, including soil conditions, connections between tree pits where possible, specifications for tree protection and a stated volume of suitable growing medium to facilitate and promote the healthy development of the proposed trees;3.	Hard landscaping, including ground surfaces, kerbs, edges ridge and flexible paving's, furniture, steps, refuse disposal points and if applicable synthetic surfaces for the podium level; 4.	Fences, walls and any other boundary treatments;5.	The materiality and design detail of Napier Road Green Street;6.	Quiet zones;7.	Outdoor play spaces and play equipment;8.	Any signage and information boards;9.	Any CCTV equipment; 10.	Allotments or community gardens 11.	Any other landscaping features forming part of the scheme; 12.	A timetable for implementation and completion of the landscaping scheme prior to first occupation of the relevant development Phase.All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the landscaping scheme approved pursuant to this Condition shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding season following the occupation of the development hereby permitted or the substantial completion of the development, whichever is the sooner. Any plants, shrubs or trees as part of the implementation of the landscaping that die or are removed, damaged or become diseased within a period of five years from the substantial completion of the relevant part of the development shall be replaced to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority in the next planting season with others of a similar size and species. Reason: to provide acceptable usable space for future occupiers and in the interests of protecting the environment, ensuring privacy, visual amenity and biodiversity.

a.	No above ground new development shall commence in a phase until a detailed scheme for any green/ brown/ blue roofs for the relevant phase, including maintenance and management arrangements, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Authorityb.	The approved details shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the relevant phase and shall be maintained thereafter. Reason: in the intrests of sustainable drainage and reduce the risk of flooding.

Prior to the commencement of superstructure works on each Phase, elevation and section drawings of the roofs showing roof mounted photovoltaic arrays, with details showing power output will be optimised through the efficient PV cell specification and layout, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The first photovoltaic arrays shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details before the first occupation of any part of the Phase and shall be retained and maintained in working order thereafter. Reason: to ensure the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon emissions.

The development shall not commence until a Flood Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating:o	The development is provided with a access/egress route within the very low hazard area (as defined by the Environment Agency's Flood Risk Assessment Guidance for New Development R&D Technical Report FD2320)o	Flood resilient and resistant measures are utilised where relevant Reason: To minimise flood risk.

Prior to occupation of the development, a Verification Report demonstrating that the approved flood risk and SuDS measures have been fully implemented shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This report must include:- As built drawings of the sustainable drainage systems including level information (if appropriate) - Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systems - Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage features - A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similarReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development.

Notwithstanding the details set out in the submitted Preliminary Drainage Strategy Alma Estate Phases 2b and 3 Flood Risk Assessment and Sustainable Drainage Strategy Revision PO3 4th December 2024, prior to the commencement of any construction work, details of the Sustainable Drainage Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and must conform with the Landscaping Strategy. The details shall include: - A final SuDS Strategy Plan, including levels; - Results of infiltration testing and correspondence with Network Rail to determine the applicability of full and partial infiltration. If infiltration is not deemed acceptable through infiltration testing an appropriate attenuation feature must be provided in line with the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy; - Final discharge rates for areas positively draining in the respective catchment areas designed to a 1 in 1 and 1 in 100 year storm event with the allowance for climate change or Qbar; - Final sizes, storage volumes, cross sections, long sections (where appropriate) and specifications of all SuDS measures the source control SuDS measures; Include calculations demonstrating functionality where relevant; - Final Management Plan for Future Maintenance outlining who will be responsible for the respective SuDS measures. Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development.

No piling shall take place until a Piling Method Statement (detailing the depth and type of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) and piling layout plan including all Thames Water wastewater assets, the local topography and clearance between the face of the pile to the face of a pipe has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority in consultation with Thames Water. Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement and piling layout plan.Reason: The proposed works will be in close proximity to underground sewerage utility infrastructure. Piling has the potential to significantly impact / cause failure of local underground sewerage utility infrastructure.

No development shall be occupied until confirmation has been provided that either:- all water network upgrades required to accommodate the additional demand to serve the development have been completed; or - a development and infrastructure phasing plan has been agreed with Thames Water to allow development to be occupied. Where a development and infrastructure phasing plan is agreed no occupation shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed development and infrastructure phasing plan. Reason: The development may lead to no / low water pressure and network reinforcement works are anticipated to be necessary to ensure that sufficient capacity is made available to accommodate additional demand anticipated from the new development.

Notwithstanding the provisions of The Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), or the provisions of The Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2020, the development hereby approved shall only be used as C3 residential and Class E, condition as identified in the approved drawings listed in condition 2, together with ancillary uses, and for no other purpose.Reason: The impacts of the development have been assessed in the context of Class C and Class E uses and uses outside this use class could have different and potentially adverse impacts that have not been assessed or mitigated.

Prior to the occupation of each phase a Decarbonisation Strategy shall be submitted and approved in writing the LPA. This shall show:a.	A commitment to investigate all viable available options for decarbonising the network and timings for doing so, e.g. waste heat sources in the area, replacement of gas-engine CHP with other technologies such as heat pumps.  b.	Evidence of existing (or planned) studies that have been undertaken and timescales for implementing the decarbonisation plans, including investigation of funding for further work from the Local Energy Accelerator (LEA) and government's Heat Network Investment Project (HNIP). c.	 A detailed plan demonstrating that the process is being monitored in order to ensure its implementation as well as a commitment to keep the GLA updated on progress. Reason: in the interest of carbon reduction and sustainability.

No development shall take place on any phase of the development (save for operations consisting of site clearance, demolition and soft-stripping of buildings, preparation of a site compound, installation of alarms and security fencing/barriers, archaeological investigations, investigations for assessing ground conditions, remedial work in respect of any contamination or other adverse ground conditions, diversion and laying of services, erection of any temporary means of enclosure and the temporary display of site notices or advertisements) unless and until all parties with a relevant legal interest in the land comprising the relevant phase of the development have entered into a planning obligation pursuant to Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) in order to ensure that the planning obligations set out in the agreement made under section 106 of the Town & Country Planning Act 1990 and other powers dated 22/12/2025 subject to which this planning permission has been granted (or any variation thereto) bind the legal interests in that phase of the development site.  Reason: at the time of this permission being granted the applicant did not have sufficient interest in the development site such that the planning obligations in the section 106 agreement would be enforceable against persons deriving title from them. Development must not commence (save for the operations outlined above) on any phase of the development site until all necessary legal interests in that phase are bound under a section 106 planning obligation.

The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than [3] years from the date of this decision.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Detailed drawings and samples of all facing materials to be used in a development phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of any façade works on each respective development phase. The details and samples shall include the following: i.	Brick bonding and brick, including banding and decorative brick panel detail (annotated plans at a scale of not less than 1:20); ii.	External windows, spandrel panels, balconies, doors, screens, louvres, grilles and balustrading (annotated plans at a scale of not less than 1:10); iii.	Depth of window reveals and soffits (annotated plans at a scale of not less than 1:20) iv. Rainwater goods (annotated plans at a scale of not less than 1:10);iv.	The details shall show all joints between different materials and components, including walls, roofs, doors, windows, sills, lintels and fasciae, balconies, soffits and balustrades, external ramps, steps, pavements, boundary walls, gates, and fences;v.	Shop fronts, entrances and openings (annotated elevations and section details at a scale of not less than 1:20); vi.	"tops" of Blocks P3A and P2G;vii.	Balconies, including any solid panels and visual screens;viii.	Sections of the landscaped areas of the scheme, showing the interface between soft and hard surface would work, the rainwater drainage strategy and associated technical solutions, and the interface between different pavements, the street, and the proposed buildings.The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details and samples so approved, shall be maintained as such thereafter, and no change therefrom shall take place without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: to ensure that the resulting appearance and construction of the development is of a high standard.Reason: to ensure that the resulting appearance and construction of the development is of a high standard.

No roof plant, equipment, or other structures, other than as shown on the plans hereby approved or approved pursuant to a condition of this permission, shall be placed on the roof(s) or external façade or be permitted to project above the roofline of any part of the buildings as shown on elevational drawings or shall be permitted to extend outside of the roof plant enclosures of any buildings hereby permitted.Details of any such equipment required for the commercial units, not shown on the approved drawings, shall first be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority and then installed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: to ensure high quality development and in the interest of visual amenity.

The total quantum of the development hereby permitted shall not exceed the quantum's listed below: (i)	Residential (Use Class C3): 723 residential units (ii)	Non-residential (Use Classes E(a), (b), (c), (e)) floorspace; 377 sqm (GIA)Reason:  In order to ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the approved plans and drawings.

Prior to commencement of development of any Phase (other than including site investigations and archaeological investigation, and erection of hoarding) a detailed Construction Logistics and Environmental Management Plan (CLEMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Development shall be thereafter carried out in accordance with the CLEMP which shall remain in force for the entire demolition and construction period. For avoidance of doubt, this condition can be discharged in the following stages: a.	Demolition works and construction up to and including ground floor slab; and, b. Construction works above ground floor slab. The CLEMP shall be informed by Construction Logistics Planning Guidance and must include as a minimum: i)	A plan showing the area to be surveyed to establish existing public highway condition:ii)	A pre-start record of the condition of the public highway identified by the plan referred to above, together with a written commitment to repair any damage caused by carrying out the developmentiii)	On-site parking and turning provision for site operatives, visitors and construction vehicles;iv)	Provision for the loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site; v)	Location of temporary offices, contractors compounds and welfare facilities on the site; vi)	Details of points of access and egress to and from the site construction traffic; vii)	Details of signage at all vehicle exits from construction site advising drivers of preferred routes viii)	The erection of maintenance of security hoarding, including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing where appropriate;ix)	Works of demolition and construction shall only take place between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 Monday to Friday and between 09.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays, and at no time on Sundays or Bank/Public Holidays; x)	Details of measures to prevent the deposition of mud and debris on the public highway, including wheel washing facilities and sheeting of vehicles transporting loose aggregates or similar materials off site;xi)	A Demolition and Construction Waste Management Plan that identifies the main waste materials, including vegetation, expected to be generated by the development, during demolition and construction, together with the measures for dealing with such materials so as to minimise waste and maximise re-use and recycling; xii)	Measure to ensure the safety of users of adjacent public highway during the construction period, in particular cyclist and pedestrians, especially at site access/egress points; xiii)	Measures to minimise emissions of dust from the site during construction written in accordance with the Mayor of London's supplementary planning guidance 'The Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' detailing how dust and emissions will be managed during demolition and construction work xiv)	Arrangements for temporary site lighting, including security lights, location and operations; xv)	Arrangements for liaising with other contractors in the vicinity of the site to maximise the potential for consolidated construction traffic movements to minimise traffic; xvi)	Procedures for maintaining good public relations, including compliant management, public consultations and liaison contact details and;xvii)	Details of a booking system for construction traffic to minimise the number of construction vehicles waiting on the public highway xviii)	Details of registration with the Considerate Contractors SchemeReason: To protect the environmental quality of the surrounding area, to safeguard the amenities of those living and working in the locality and in the interest of highway safety.

No part of the residential or commercial accommodation hereby permitted in any Phase shall be occupied until a Waste Management Strategy showing the full details of the waste and recycling facilities, including management of storage areas, internal collections and collection for the site for those accommodations, has been submitted and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The waste and recycling facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the relevant residential or commercial element. They shall be retained throughout the lifetime of the development and shall be used for no other purposes. Reason: to encourage the sustainable management of waste, to ensure acceptable living conditions for future occupiers in the interests of visual amenity.

a) Prior to first occupation of each Phase, a detailed Whole Life-Cycle Carbon assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, demonstrating that the Whole Life Cycle Carbon emissions savings of the development are secured and achieve the benchmarks set out in the Mayor of London's Whole Life-Cycle Assessment Guidance. The assessment shall include details of measures to reduce carbon emissions throughout the whole life cycle of the development and provide calculations in line with the Mayor's Guidance.b) Within 8 weeks of completion of the development hereby approved the post construction tab of the GLA's whole life carbon assessment template should be completed accurately and in its entirety in line with the GLA's Whole Life Carbon Assessment Guidance. The post-construction assessment should prove an update of the information submitted at the planning stage, including the whole life carbon emissions figures for all life cycle -modules based on the actual materials, products and systems use. This should be submitted to the GLA at: ZeroCarbonPlanning@london.gov.uk , along with any supporting evidence as per the guidance. Confirmation of submission to the GLA shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to maximise on-site carbon dioxide savings.
